q: `records.lock().unwrap()` (testprovider.rs:206) returns a MutexGuard. When does the lock release?
options: When the guard is dropped — at the end of its scope
When the program exits
After a fixed timeout
On the next lock() call
explanation: Locks are scope-bound RAII; no program-exit dependency.
There's no timeout on std Mutex::lock — it blocks indefinitely.
A second lock() call waits; it doesn't release anything.

q: Holding a `std::sync::MutexGuard` across an `.await` in a Send-required future fails to compile because:
options: MutexGuard is not Send, so the future can't be moved between threads while it holds locked state
Tokio forbids std Mutex entirely
The guard becomes unusable after await (turns into &mut)
Rust deallocates locked state on suspension
explanation: std Mutex is fine in tokio — held only for short non-await sections.
Guards remain usable; it's the Send trait the compiler checks.
Suspension doesn't deallocate; the Send requirement is what fails.

q: Why does TestProvider compute `hash_input(messages)` OUTSIDE the records lock?
options: Hashing inside the lock would serialize all concurrent streams behind one big critical section
Hashing requires the lock held for correctness
hash_input can't run while the HashMap exists
To prevent deadlocks with tokio's Mutex
explanation: Correctness only needs the lock around the map read/write, not around pure computation.
Hashing is independent of the map; it can run before taking it.
There's no interaction with tokio Mutex here — it's std Mutex synchronization cost that matters.

q: `MessageStream = Pin<Box<dyn Stream<Item = Result<(Option<Message>, Option<ProviderUsage>), ProviderError>> + Send>>` — the `Option`s around Message/ProviderUsage exist because:
options: Streams may yield usage-only or finish with no final message, so each slot can be absent per item
Provider messages are often null in JSON
Rust requires every stream item be an Option
It marks the stream as possibly empty of all items
explanation: The Option shapes matter per-item (message vs usage vs both), not JSON nulls.
Items can be any type; Option-ness here is modeled deliberately.
Both slots are independently optional — it's not about the whole stream being empty.
